sources.title: Data from: A meta-analysis of global avian survival across species and latitude
sources.note: ELEscholer2020_data.csv, X=695, Parker et al. (2006), Colonche Hills, Ecuador; row lists apparent survival 0.86, SE 0.10, mark-recapture, duration 6 years. Used for the dataset mass estimate only; it does not support typical lifespan.

taxonomy.note: Both providers return this exact species at species rank; GBIF usage key 2493957 and iNaturalist taxon 597354 checked 2026-11-01.

range.note: Scope is limited to requested CO. Wikipedia distribution describes the natural montane range extending through the Andes and to Venezuela and Bolivia; Colombia lies in that range. The record does not claim a complete global country list.

behavior.note: Species-local copy of the shared perching-songbird tree. Movement and food fit: hop on ground/low vegetation, eat invertebrates, powered flight, perching, alarm/flee, night shelter. The Colombia breeding gate uses explicit months [12,1,2,3,4,5,6], the union of the main April-June Colombian period and the Huila December-May observations. Night branch exits to sheltered rest. Daytime song is allowed throughout daylight, matching the account that it sings year-round and through the day. No claim is made about nesting outside Colombia because this record only has a CO activity curve.

look.note: Authored stylized palette and proportions from the described gray-brown plumage, pale gray breast and long gray-white supercilium; mesh ratios are judgement.

activity.CO.note: Country-level GBIF occurrence query for accepted species key 2493957, present human observations, no flagged geospatial issue, month facet and CC0/CC BY only. 88,046 records overall, of which 87,503 have a month (543 do not); all twelve month counts are nonzero (Jan-Dec: 8662, 8308, 8135, 5799, 8837, 5549, 6546, 6272, 5495, 8166, 7844, 7890). iNaturalist tier C (329 records; includes NC licences) was excluded because GBIF tier A alone exceeds threshold.

seasonal.strategy.note: Resident, year-round singing and activity: Wikipedia Behavior and Vocalization sections state year-round song; no migration evidence identified for the requested country.

seasonal.phases.note: Aves del Valle de Sibundoy p. 293 reports Colombian breeding primarily April-June and additional Huila records December-May. This species-specific calendar source is CC BY-NC 4.0 and was used as a last resort after Wikipedia (CC BY-SA) and provider records gave no Colombia-specific dates; keep the NC provenance limited to these phase dates.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Adult, egg and juvenile stages are standard bird stages; juvenile scale 0.75 is an authored preview judgement. Nest requirement maps to the globular nest with a chamber and downward-facing entrance.

traits.mass_kg.note: ELEscholer2020_data.csv row X=695 reports mass 16.19 g; converted to kilograms by dividing by 1000. This meta-analysis row also reports 0.86 apparent annual adult survival, SE 0.10; that survival statistic is not used as lifespan because it confounds death and permanent emigration.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the stated nominate-subspecies range 10 to 11.5 cm, converted to metres: (10+11.5)/2/100 = 0.1075 m.

traits.size_class.note: Tiny follows the measured mass 0.01619 kg, below the schema threshold of 0.05 kg.

traits.diet.note: The source says the diet appears solely invertebrate; 1.0 represents that qualitative statement as an authored model allocation.

traits.social.note: Source says birds forage singly or in small groups. Pair and size bound [1,4] are authored simulation abstractions, not measured demographic values.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Daytime activity and singing through the day.

traits.defense.note: Skulking low in dense vegetation and difficult to see; mapped to Hide.

traits.wariness.note: Authored judgement based on the source describing a skulking, often unseen bird.

habitat.use.note: The source places it in humid montane forest and describes foraging from the ground to low vegetation; 55/45 split is an authored placement estimate.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Dense low vegetation is used as the closest available roost/shelter tag.

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrates are the stated diet. Shelter, perch and nest resource weights are authored placement estimates based on dense vegetation, perching and globular nest description.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Forest species with no garden use stated; Avoider and the numeric light tolerance are authored placement judgments.

vocalizations.song.note: Wikipedia Vocalization section says songs are loud, repeated musical phrases and heard virtually year-round through the day.
